note: Written from reading the chapter, before any event, claim or link was written. Verdicts are what the chapter establishes, not what the novel later reveals.
key_corrections: told_late: was [], now [e-mina-night, e-mina-harbour]. I forgot that Mina's night and morning of the storm happen before the 9 August dispatch but are told after it (P63-P64 against P16-P17). The text order is not the story order here, which is the point of the check.
A second mismatch was my encoding, not the key: the dateline 'Whitby' (P16) sat in the dispatch event, so the mastiff, told in P17, looked late. The dateline now belongs to the event before.

verdict_at for c-stranger-aboard and c-mate-killed-crew: my four entries were the captain's view in the voyage, but verdict_at is the record's view, and every voyage event enters the record when the log is read (e-log-read). They are now two sets: verdict_at (record time: both open once the log is read) and verdict_for (the captain's own, from what he knew then). The model gained verdict_for because of this.

post_hoc.note: The last knows_at entry (the sleepwalker does not know her own walk) was added after the encoding, because the party rule said she did. Not blind.

post_hoc_knows3: knows3 (knows / possibly / no) added after the crowd problem was found in round three (nobody in a crowd could be asked individually); written from the text before pinning: the boat captains are in the sunset assemblage with the crowd, the fisherman was with the afternoon gossips, the coal merchant appears only the next morning.
post_hoc_gaps: gaps added in round four with time.ties. Written from the text first: under the 9 August reading the dog is found about four hours after the leap (330-80 minutes after midnight), under the 8 August reading about 28 hours; the same-epoch pair needs no tie.
